Hero.title: Hisho (飛翔)
Hero.tagline: Next-generation trading software built for the Japanese stock market.

About.title: Our Mission
About.description: We are developing an innovative trading platform tailored specifically for Japan's stock market. Our goal is to provide an intuitive, high-speed, and reliable trading environment to help investors soar.

Timeline.title: Launch Timeline
Timeline.description: Currently in development. Targeting launch in Q2–Q3 2027.

Ecommerce.title: E-commerce Services
Ecommerce.description: In addition to our trading system, we are planning to offer seamless e-commerce services in the future.

Rules.title: Exam Rules & Consent
Rules.rule1: You have 2 hours. The countdown begins when you select Start, and the exam automatically closes and submits at zero.
Rules.rule2: AI tools are strictly forbidden. Copy and paste is disabled throughout the exam.
Rules.rule3: We review your written answers, Figma design work, and videos together. Export each Figma deliverable as a PDF or PNG before uploading.
Rules.rule4: If selected, the position is a paid 2-month internship at a salary of ¥80,000.
Rules.rule5: If our AI-detection process finds evidence that AI was used, the candidate will be blacklisted from this exam AND from any future position at the company.
Rules.checkbox: I have read and understood the rules above.

AntiCheat.warning: Copy/paste is disabled during this exam.

Exam.sectionBBrief: Design a mobile experience that helps a first-time investor in Japan review a stock and place an order with confidence. Work in one Figma file, then export one PDF or PNG for each deliverable below (20 MB maximum per file).
Exam.sectionCNote: Upload MP4, MOV, or WebM videos (500 MB maximum each). Allow enough time for uploads to complete before the countdown ends.

questions.q1: Walk us through your design process, from receiving a problem to delivering a design.
questions.q2: How would you learn what first-time investors in Japan find confusing about a trading app?
questions.q3: What questions would you ask a beginner during a user interview?
questions.q4: How would you turn user interview findings into design priorities?
questions.q5: How would you make a stock detail screen useful to both beginners and experienced investors?
questions.q6: How would you explain market orders and limit orders in the interface without overwhelming a beginner?
questions.q7: What information should users see before confirming a stock order, and why?
questions.q8: How would you help users understand fees, price changes, and potential risk?
questions.q9: How would you design an error message when an order cannot be placed?
questions.q10: What accessibility checks would you make for a mobile trading app?
questions.q11: What would you consider when designing this experience specifically for users in Japan?
questions.q12: How do you keep buttons, forms, and other components consistent across screens?
questions.q13: Tell us about feedback that changed one of your designs. How did you respond?
questions.q14: What would you provide to developers when handing off a Figma design?
questions.q15: If a design could encourage risky trading, how would you raise the concern and improve it?
questions.q16: You have three usability issues but time to fix only one. How would you decide which to address first?
questions.q17: How would you test whether a first-time investor understands your order review screen?
questions.q18: After your design launches, what evidence would tell you it improved the user experience?
questions.q19: Create a simple user flow from viewing a stock to reviewing and confirming an order. Mark one point where a user might make a mistake.
questions.q20: Create low-fidelity wireframes for the stock detail and order review screens.
questions.q21: Turn the order review wireframe into a high-fidelity mobile screen. Show the price, quantity, estimated total, and primary action clearly.
questions.q22: Design an error state and a successful order confirmation state.
questions.q23: Add brief Figma annotations explaining three important design choices, including how the design helps prevent an accidental order.
questions.q24: Please record and upload a short video (approximately 1 minute) introducing yourself. Explain why we should offer you this internship and why you believe you are the right fit for this position. You must present entirely in English.
questions.q25: Please record and upload a split-screen video explaining your Final Project submission: why you chose to build this specific project over other options, what its practical use is, and how you went about developing it. The video must be split-screen, with one side showing a live walkthrough of your project and the other side showing your face as you speak. You must present entirely in English.
